name: iem-ui
description: IEM AG website and CMS dashboard (React + Tailwind + Vite)

scripts.// typecheck: Three programs: the app (browser types only), the unit tests (which read files off disk and need Node), and the Playwright suite. The third was added after e2e/ turned out to be typechecked by nobody — Playwright transpiles without checking, so a mistake there surfaced as a runtime failure partway through a fifteen-minute run.
scripts.// checks: The gates. `verify` is what to run before a commit and what CI should run.
scripts.// format: Prettier is configured but the existing tree is NOT formatted, and `format` is deliberately left out of `verify`. Running it today rewrites 74 files: it would bury every future diff, destroy `git blame` on a codebase whose comments are its main documentation, and reflow hand-aligned blocks that were set that way on purpose. Use it on a file you are already rewriting, not across the repo. Reformatting everything is a decision to take once, on its own commit, with nothing else in it.
scripts.// verify: Both halves: the site and the API each have their own typecheck and test run. Needs nothing running and finishes in seconds — this is the pre-commit gate.
scripts.verify: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test && npm --prefix server run typecheck && npm --prefix server run test
scripts.// e2e: Playwright: the real dashboard in a real browser, at three widths, in both themes, with an axe pass. It needs `npm run dev`, `npm run server:dev` and a seeded database already running, which is why it is NOT in `verify` — a gate that fails on a machine with no database is a gate people learn to skip. Run it before a release, or after anything that touches the shell, the theme or the routes.
scripts.// e2e:backup: Backup and recovery, including the RECOVERY DRILL — a real pg_dump, a real pg_restore into an isolated database, and the validation that proves the artifact becomes a database an application can read. Needs pg_dump/pg_restore on PATH or PG_BIN_PATH set; skips with a message otherwise. Run it on its own: it writes hundreds of megabytes and creates and drops a database, which distorts anything measured beside it.
scripts.// mail:catcher: A real SMTP server for development and for `e2e:mail`, so the last hop of the notification chain is actually exercised rather than resolving to SKIPPED. Mailpit listens on 1025 (SMTP) and 8025 (HTTP API); the E2E spec asks that API whether a message arrived, which is what proves an SMTP transaction happened rather than that a library call returned. It is a DEVELOPMENT dependency and never a production one — nothing in the application knows it exists, it is reached only through the ordinary `mail.smtpHost` setting. Fetch it once with `mail:catcher:install`; `var/` is gitignored, so the binary is not committed.
scripts.// verify:all: Everything, for a release. Assumes the servers are up.
scripts.verify:all: npm run verify && npm run e2e
scripts.// server: The API lives in server/ and has its own package.json and node_modules.
scripts.server:build: node scripts/stamp-build.mjs && npm --prefix server run build
scripts.// setup: One-time: install the API, create the schema, fill it from the site's own content.
scripts.setup: npm run server:install && npm run db:migrate && npm run server:seed
